M01.reason: With && the (RESP && ERR) term is never true, so beats_left, address and error-state data never update after an R handshake. Multi-beat reads never reach the last beat, so RLAST is never raised and the beat count and addresses are wrong.

M02.reason: WREADY is high in every state except WDAT (and in DRAIN). It is high before AW is accepted and low when W data is expected, which breaks WREADY gating and the W beat count.

M03.reason: The AWSIZE>2 check now sets w_aw_valid=1 instead of 0. Writes with unsupported size 3..7 are accepted and sent to APB instead of being drained and answered with SLVERR.

M04.reason: The REQ state advances on !i_req_ready. The write sequencer moves to WAIT before the APB controller accepts the beat, and it stalls once the controller accepts it. APB writes are lost or hang.

M05.reason: The WRAP alignment test is inverted. Legal aligned WRAP writes are rejected with SLVERR and no APB access, while unaligned ones are accepted.

M06.reason: req_ready is given when the APB FSM is not IDLE, not when it is IDLE. Payload capture needs req_ready in IDLE, so APB SETUP starts without a captured payload, and the sequencer handshake happens in the wrong phase.

M07.reason: The response (rsp_valid, data, err) is latched when the APB FSM is not in ACCESS but PREADY is high. PRDATA and PSLVERR are not captured at the true completion, so R and B responses are lost or wrong.

M08.reason: The W capture, beats_left decrement and address advance now fire when WDAT or wvalid is true. Data, strobes and address are captured or consumed without a W handshake, or in non-WDAT states, so PWDATA, PSTRB and the beat count are corrupted.

M09.reason: Line 165 is only the default assignment ahead of the case on reg_fsm_apb_current_state. Every case branch (SETUP, ACCESS and default) assigns o_apb_pwrite again, so the initial 1 never reaches the port.

M10.reason: The default of w_ar_valid becomes 0 and nothing sets it back to 1. Every read is treated as unsupported, so legal reads get SLVERR with no APB access.

M11.reason: Write transfers latch pwrite=0, so they appear on APB as reads. The write response goes to the read response path and the AXI write never completes correctly.

M12.reason: The default of o_axi_rvalid becomes 1 and is never cleared. RVALID is high in IDLE, REQ and WAIT and during reset, giving spurious R beats.

M13.reason: WREADY needs state==WDAT and state==DRAIN at once, which never happens. WREADY is never raised, so write data is never accepted and writes hang.

M14.reason: turn_rd is only read in the ctrl IDLE state. The controller leaves ACTRD only through i_rd_done, and then both versions clear turn_rd. The mutant also clears it early while waiting in ACTRD, but that value is never observed. The else-if write branch is not affected because rd_done never occurs outside ACTRD.

M15.reason: The APB start needs both read and write grants and requests at once, which never happens. APB SETUP never begins and every transfer hangs.

M16.reason: The beat counter and address update only on the last beat instead of on every non-last beat. Multi-beat reads do not advance the address or count, so the address sequence and RLAST position are wrong.

M17.reason: The read APB request valid is asserted in every state except REQ. The APB read is not requested in REQ, so legal reads stall or issue spurious requests.

M18.reason: The IDLE branch is inverted. Valid reads go to the ERR state (SLVERR beats, no APB) and invalid reads go to the APB REQ path.

M19.reason: rd_done fires on any R handshake or on RLAST alone. The owner is released after every beat, or before RREADY on the last beat, so another transaction can start mid-burst.

M20.reason: wr_ready stays 0 in IDLE, so the controller never moves GRW to ACTWR and never sees wr_done. After the first write the controller stays in GRW, the turn never flips, and reads are starved.

M21.reason: The invalid-WRAP test uses && instead of ||. WRAP with a bad length (not 2/4/8/16 beats) but aligned, or with a good length but unaligned, is now accepted instead of rejected. The bad-length case is an unsupported burst under the spec, so the mutant issues APB for it instead of SLVERR.

M22.reason: The write error is accumulated only when not in WAIT. rsp_valid only arrives in WAIT, so PSLVERR on APB writes is never recorded and BRESP is OKAY instead of SLVERR.

M23.reason: The AW beat count gets a 1 prefix, adding 256 to the 9-bit sum. The INCR total byte count for the 4-KiB check is wrong, so legal INCR writes are rejected as 4-KiB crossings.

M24.reason: DRAIN exits when the last-beat condition is false. The reject path leaves DRAIN right away and gives B before all AWLEN+1 W beats are drained, and the beat count goes wrong.

M25.reason: The cache check is now cache==0 && cache!=1. AWCACHE=0000 (legal) is rejected, and illegal values such as 0010 are accepted and sent to APB.

M26.reason: The turn bit is inverted, so AW wins the first tie after reset and the preference alternates the wrong way.

M27.reason: Payload capture requires the APB FSM not to be IDLE, but req_ready is only high in IDLE. Address, data, strobe and PPROT are never latched, so PADDR and PPROT stay 0.

M28.reason: wr_done fires as soon as BVALID is high, even without BREADY. The owner is released while B is still pending, so a new transaction can start during B backpressure.

M29.reason: In the idle/default branch PENABLE becomes 1 while PSEL is 0, so PENABLE is high without PSEL and in reset.

M30.reason: rd_ready stays 0 in IDLE, so the controller never leaves GRD to ACTRD and never sees rd_done. After the first read the controller stays in GRD, the turn never flips, and writes are starved.

M31.reason: PSEL is 0 during the ACCESS phase, so PENABLE is high without PSEL. The APB access phase is wrong.

M32.reason: The AR beat count gets a 1 prefix, adding 256. The INCR total byte count for the 4-KiB check is wrong, so legal INCR reads are rejected as 4-KiB crossings.

M33.reason: The invalid-WRAP test uses && instead of ||. WRAP writes with a bad length (not 2/4/8/16 beats) but aligned, or with a good length but unaligned, are now accepted instead of rejected. The bad-length case is an unsupported burst under the spec, so the mutant issues APB writes for it instead of SLVERR.

M34.reason: APB SETUP now starts whenever gnt_rd is high or rd_req_valid is high, even with no read request (for example during R backpressure, or in an unsupported read). This produces spurious APB transfers.

M35.reason: The WRAP next-address condition is inverted. A WRAP read wraps when it should not and increments across the wrap boundary, so the APB addresses are wrong.

M36.reason: RVALID/RLAST are driven in RESP and in every state except ERR. Unsupported reads never present their SLVERR beats, and RVALID is high in IDLE, REQ and WAIT.
